mintAuthority.summary: CGO's sole authored deployment is the canonical XDC Goldtoken, and its CGOController is a native issuance router rather than a bridge adapter. The token owner is CGOController 0x21f74fbf81d68291704805d085982000babbf096. At the cutoff, the controller's owner, initiator, executor, and minter-wallet addresses all resolved to the same immediate 2-of-4 Safe at 0xc639b48ea44e94f1a69da11974a29e6ddb8c6fa1. Native minting requires one Safe transaction to initiate a unique bar/warrant pair and a second Safe transaction to mint exactly 1,000 CGO, but there is no cumulative or time-window cap. The Safe can immediately replace all operational addresses or transfer token ownership to a new address, bypassing the controller's per-operation bound and exposing the token's uncapped owner-only mint function. No bridge representation or bridge administrator is evidenced, so these native route checks are not bridge risk.

controls.label: CGO 2/4 Safe mint and ownership authority
controls.capDescription: The normal controller route mints exactly 1,000 CGO per completed bar/warrant operation, but has no cumulative or time-window cap. The same Safe can transfer token ownership to an arbitrary new owner that can call Goldtoken.mint(address,uint256) without the controller bound.
bypassSurfaces: CGOController.transferCgoOwnership(newOwner) lets the Safe replace the controller as token owner; the new owner can then call the token's uncapped mint(address,uint256) directly.
controls.evidence: At XDC block 104889953, CGOController.owner(), initiatorAddr(), executorAddr(), and minterWalletAddr() all returned 0xc639b48ea44e94f1a69da11974a29e6ddb8c6fa1. The Safe returned four owners, threshold 2, VERSION 1.3.0, no enabled modules, zero guard, fallback handler 0xf48f2b2d2a534e402487b3ee7c18c33aec0fe5e4, and singleton 0x3e5c63644e683549055b9be8653de26e0b4cd36e. All four owners had empty bytecode. Native issuance checks retained from the legacy routeChecks block: the same Safe holds controller owner, initiator, executor, and minter-wallet authority; initiation and execution require separate Safe transactions; CGOController.mint requires amount == 1000 and a previously initiated unique bar/warrant pair; no aggregate supply cap, per-period limit, or enforced delay exists; and the immutable token/controller path can still be bypassed by replacing operational addresses or transferring token ownership. These are native bar/warrant issuance constraints, not bridge machinery.

controls.label: Immutable CGOController two-step mint router
controls.capDescription: Fixed code requires initiation followed by execution and exactly 1,000 CGO per bar/warrant operation; ultimate authority remains the controller-owning Safe.
controls.evidence: CGOController is a source-verified direct deployment. Its EIP-1967 implementation, admin, and beacon slots are zero. It owns the Goldtoken and calls owner-only mint only after a current initiator creates a bar/warrant request and the current executor completes it.

review.evidence: At XDC block 104889953, Goldtoken 0x8f9920283470f52128bf11b0c14e798be704fd15 and CGOController 0x21f74fbf81d68291704805d085982000babbf096 were source-verified direct deployments with zero EIP-1967 implementation, admin, and beacon slots. The controller owned the token, and its owner, initiator, executor, and minter-wallet fields all resolved to the same immediate 2-of-4 Safe 0xc639b48ea44e94f1a69da11974a29e6ddb8c6fa1. The controller's fixed 1,000-CGO operation bound had no cumulative cap and could be bypassed by the Safe transferring token ownership to a new uncapped minter. Mint-tier review (2026-07-15): No credible independent reserve-to-liability reconciliation exists. The latest posted routine-audit document, dated 2026-02-26, is a one-page ComTech FZCO self-signed confirmation of 39 kg of gold and does not reconcile CGO supply; no independent attestor or recurring assurance cadence is identified. DMCC Tradeflow and free-zone registration are commodity-title and commercial records, not prudential stablecoin-issuer supervision. Economic-posture fields reviewed 2026-08-15: the issuer Safe can bypass the per-operation amount by transferring token ownership to an uncapped minter; self-signed stock letters do not reconcile supply and DMCC records are not prudential supervision. Reconciliation review (2026-08-15): ComTech's dated 26 February 2026 stock letter reports 39 kg of gold but does not reconcile CGO token liabilities against that reserve; no independent recurring reserve-to-supply attestation or live reconciliation was found, so reconciliation remains unknown. Boundary migration (2026-08-16): the bar/warrant checks are native issuance constraints on the sole canonical XDC deployment, not bridge machinery. No bridge representation, bridge administrator, or bridgeRouteRisk route is evidenced for CGO.
